# @aegis_trust/sdk

> The trust layer for AI agents — control what data agents can see, based on declared purpose. TypeScript / Node port of aegis-trust (PyPI).

@aegis_trust/sdk is a TypeScript / Node.js SDK that filters what AI agents see when calling your data-fetching functions. One wrapper declares the purpose; the SDK enforces field-level access control. Local-first, no infrastructure required, no telemetry.

## Quick Start

```
npm install @aegis_trust/sdk
```

```typescript
import { shield } from "@aegis_trust/sdk";

const getCustomer = shield({
  purpose: "customer_support",
  scope: ["name", "issue"],
})((id: number) => db.get(id));

// Agent sees only { name: ..., issue: ... }
```

## Key Concepts

- purpose: Why the agent needs this data (e.g. "customer_support", "billing")
- scope: Whitelist of fields the agent is allowed to see
- denyFields: Blacklist alternative — hide listed fields, keep the rest
- Dot-notation: scope: ["name", "profile.age"] for nested paths
- aegis.yaml: Centralize policies in a single config file (optional, requires `npm install yaml`)
- Vitest helpers: useShieldHistory, assertShieldBlocked, assertShieldPassed for testing
- Mode.LITE / FULL / AUTO: in-process filter / full audit chain (via aegis-core) / auto-detect

## Use Cases

- AI customer support: the agent sees ticket text, never PII
- LLM tool calling (MCP / FastMCP / Vercel AI SDK): wrap tool functions with `shield(...)`
- Billing / finance agents: `scope: ["plan", "status"]` or `denyFields: ["card", "ssn"]`
- Compliance: declared purpose produces an audit trail of what each agent was permitted to see

## Optional Extras

- `npm install yaml` — enable aegis.yaml policy file support
- For production deployments with enterprise controls and platform-managed policy orchestration, email contact@aegisagentcontrol.com
